summary: Backend-only testing of Cancel Subscription (Pending Expiry) feature. 18/19 pytest cases pass (94.7%). Happy path, idempotency, RBAC (staff blocked), access preservation post-cancel, undo flow, platform stats.cancelled_pending counter, platform tenant list + detail cancellation_pending surfacing, and cannot-cancel-expired all PASS. One real gap found: suspended tenant (is_active=false) can still be cancelled — endpoint uses require_admin without an is_active guard and tenant_status() never maps is_active→'suspended'. Glow Up tenant state restored to non-cancelled at end of suite.

minor.issue: Suspended tenants (is_active=false) can still cancel subscription. Endpoint uses require_admin (no is_active check) and core.tenant_status() only derives status from subscription_status/end_date, never 'suspended'. Review request expected 400/403. Fix: switch to require_admin_active OR add explicit is_active guard at top of cancel_my_subscription.

action_items: Enforce suspended-tenant guard in POST /api/tenants/me/cancel-subscription. Preferred: change dependency from require_admin to require_admin_active (auto-blocks is_active=False with 403 'Tenant is suspended' via check_subscription). Alternative: add `if not tenant.get('is_active', True): raise HTTPException(400, 'Cannot cancel a suspended subscription')` after loading the tenant.
Optional: consider surfacing is_active=False as status='suspended' in tenant_status() so the same guard `if st['status'] in ('expired','suspended','cancelled')` catches it.
critical_code_review_comments: cancel_my_subscription uses require_admin (role-only), not require_admin_active. This means suspended/expired tenants can still hit the endpoint; the endpoint mitigates 'expired' via tenant_status() but NOT 'suspended' (is_active=false), which tenant_status never derives.
cancelled_by is stored as user['email'] || user['id'] — fine, but ensure this field is always trustworthy (email is; consider adding it to JWT claims for defence-in-depth, though not required now).
seed_data_creation: None. Only mutated glowup-tenant-0001 cancellation fields temporarily; teardown restores state (cancellation cleared, is_active=true, subscription_status/active preserved).
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_iter20_cancel_subscription.py is idempotent and self-cleaning (autouse module fixture wipes cancellation on entry & exit). Safe to re-run alongside other iter regression suites. The one failing test (TestCancelInvalidStates::test_cannot_cancel_suspended) will start passing once main agent adds an is_active/suspended guard to cancel_my_subscription.
rca_of_issue: Bug: 'Cannot cancel a suspended tenant' requirement is not enforced. Reproduction: (1) as platform admin, POST /api/platform/tenants/glowup-tenant-0001/subscription {is_active:false}; (2) as glowup owner, POST /api/tenants/me/cancel-subscription → returns 200 with cancellation_pending=true (expected 400/403). Root cause: routes/tenants.py:cancel_my_subscription depends on require_admin (role check only) and its explicit block-list `if st['status'] in ('expired','suspended','cancelled')` never fires because core.tenant_status() ignores tenant.is_active — it only derives status from subscription_status/end_date. Mitigation: switch dependency to require_admin_active (which invokes check_subscription that returns 403 for is_active=False), or add `if not tenant.get('is_active', True): raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail='Cannot cancel a suspended subscription. Please contact support.')` immediately after load_tenant().
